summary: Iteration 63 — Editorial Relationship CRM™ (Phase R-CRM-2) backend validated 100% GREEN (17/17 pytest, ~30s). Migration 041 fully applied — all 5 new tables (relationship_engagement_signals, relationship_affinities, relationship_projects, relationship_inspirations, relationship_material_affinities, account_markets) and the relationship_intelligence_v view are reachable via API. Verified: (1) GET /api/relationships/lookups returns the 10 canonical Editorial Journey stages (discovery, inspiration, editorial_engagement, project_conversation, material_exploration, strategic_direction, specification, proposal, active_collaboration, long_term_relationship) with metadata.canonical=true AND metadata.editorial_journey=true (legacy stages coexist as designed — non-breaking). (2) POST /api/relationships/accounts/{aid}/engagement with signal_type='viewed_article', editorial_register='Ceremonial Hospitality', atmosphere_tags=['mediterranean','stone'], cta_intent='private_consultation', signal_weight=1.5 returns 201 with full signal envelope (id, account_id, occurred_at). (3) GET engagement lists newest-first and ?signal_type=viewed_article filter works. (4) POST .../affinities/recompute aggregates the heuristic into preferred_atmosphere='mediterranean', preferred_cta_intent='private_consultation', preferred_editorial_register='Ceremonial Hospitality', signal_count_total>0, computed_at populated — deterministic. (5) GET .../affinities returns the same snapshot (idempotent read). (6) Project link POST 201 → GET lists → DELETE 204 → GET no longer contains. (7) Inspiration link POST 201 → GET lists → DELETE 204 round-trip. (8) Material-affinities upsert idempotent on (account_id,material_id) — re-POST with different score UPDATES (not duplicates) the row. (9) Account ↔ market: first POST {is_primary:true} marks primary AND updates accounts.market_id pointer; second POST with different market_id and is_primary:true demotes the first to is_primary=false. (10) GET /api/relationships/intelligence returns rows with all 9 documented fields (account_id, account_name, signal_count_total, signal_count_30d, signal_count_7d, linked_project_count, linked_inspiration_count, material_affinity_count, market_count); ?journey_stage and ?market_id filters accepted. (11) Regression R-CRM-1 endpoints (GET /accounts, GET /accounts/{id}, POST /accounts/{id}/stage) still functional, no Mongo _id leak, no breaking changes.

minor.issue: No DELETE endpoint exposed for account_markets rows — once a market is linked, callers cannot unlink it via API (only demote by linking another market as primary). Consider adding DELETE /api/relationships/accounts/{aid}/markets/{mid}.
No DELETE endpoint for individual engagement signals. Test signals will accumulate over time on the demo account. Consider adding DELETE for tenancy hygiene OR a tenant-scoped purge.

On unique-violation (re-linking same project_id+role) the code raises HTTPException(409, f'Already linked: {e}') — leaks the raw DB exception string into the API response. Sanitize to a stable message.

action_items: (LOW) Add DELETE /api/relationships/accounts/{aid}/markets/{mid} so the inverse of the link operation is reachable via API (parity with projects/inspirations endpoints).
(LOW) Consider exposing DELETE for engagement signals (or a bulk admin purge) so test data and demo state can be reset without DB access.
(NITPICK) routers/relationships.py:881 `raise HTTPException(409, f'Already linked: {e}')` — strip the embedded exception text from the user-facing message to avoid leaking PostgREST error envelopes.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/relationships.py is now 1027 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into relationships_core.py (R-CRM-1: accounts/contacts/interactions/actions/style/lookups) and relationships_editorial.py (R-CRM-2: engagement/affinities/projects/inspirations/material/markets/intelligence). The Pydantic models for R-CRM-2 are clustered at line 654-699 so the seam is natural.

All R-CRM-2 endpoints are synchronous (def, not async def) while doing network I/O to Supabase. This is consistent with the rest of the file but blocks the event loop. Either convert the whole router to async with httpx, or run handlers in a thread pool — currently every request blocks a worker.

recompute_affinities() loads up to 2000 signals per account in a single sync call and recomputes a Counter — fine for now but at scale move to a materialized table refresh or background worker. The endpoint should also be guarded by P_RELATIONSHIPS_WRITE (currently unguarded — anyone with a valid session can trigger recompute on any account in their tenant).

Permission decorators (require_permission) are NOT applied to any of the 13 new R-CRM-2 endpoints. Per /app/memory/test_credentials.md, business-data routes should be permission-guarded. A `designer` role currently can POST engagement signals and recompute affinities — review whether this matches the intended editorial role matrix.

log_engagement_signal() updates accounts.last_activity_at without filtering on tenant_id in the UPDATE clause (line 729: `.eq('id', aid)`). Although _assert_account_owned() already checked ownership, defence-in-depth says always include tenant_id on writes — same pattern as _touch_account() above which DOES include `.eq('tenant_id', tid)`.

upsert_account_market() promotes a market to primary by first running `update({'is_primary': False}).eq('account_id', aid)` — this is missing `.eq('tenant_id', tid)` (line 991). Low risk because account_id is already tenant-scoped, but inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.

Inspiration / project link POST endpoints catch broad `Exception` and rewrap as 409 — masks any real DB error (constraint failure vs network blip vs schema drift). Narrow to PostgrestAPIError or check the error code before raising 409.

The minor issues are missing DELETE endpoints (markets, engagement signals) and a 409 error-message leak when re-linking a project — all LOW priority. Code-review comments flag (a) file size (1027 lines, split recommended), (b) missing permission decorators on new endpoints, (c) tenant_id missing on some UPDATE writes (defence-in-depth, not a current vulnerability since _assert_account_owned gates the path), and (d) blocking sync handlers doing network I/O.
